modules.module_title: Select the crop/ plant and site for hydroponic farming

pcs.pc_description: select the appropriate crops/ plants suitable for hydroponics farming based on priority and market demand
select a location with the required temperature and sunlight exposure, suitable to the selected plant/ crop variety
ensure the availability of various inputs such as water, electricity, fertilisers and labour for hydroponic farming
prepare the tabulation of the crop, following the recommended process
select the appropriate growth medium for seed germination, ensuring the medium has the required characteristics such as moderate fertility, water holding capacity, good aeration capacity, etc.
use coco peat, rice husk, and sand peat to raise seedlings, avoiding the use of any medium to grow agronomical crops such as wheat, paddy, maize, barley, oat, etc. for nursery and fodder purposes
sterilise the growing medium before use, according to the applicable sterilisation limit
select nursery containers for the growth of plants such as clay pots, plastic pots, or trays, as required
clean and sterilise the pots and trays before sowing seeds
apply the nutrient solution in the recommended quantity to the trays and pots and sow the seeds
maintain seedlings in the trays and pots for the recommended duration, protecting them from pests and disease and ensuring effective nutrient management
harvest the seedlings at the appropriate stage of their growth to be transplanted in the appropriate hydroponic system
select the appropriate hydroponic technique for growing quality medium to obtain quality produce with the required colour, appearance, etc.

select different kinds of substrates to be used for the cultivation of vegetables and fruits, such as lava rocks, clay pebbles, coco peat, ensuring the substrate does not contain excess salt or other elements that are harmful to plants
select an appropriate nutrient circulation method such as the Nutrient Film Technique, Deep Flow Technique (DFT), wick system, water culture, EBB and Flow, drip system, etc.
create holes in Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipes for the Deep Flow Technique (DFT) and insert plants placed in plastic net pots, in the holes made in PVC pipes
use the recommended flooring material in the hydroponic farm, that is capable of soaking in any spillage and leakages
adopt the Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) for leafy plants for their faster growth
sterilise the growing medium before use
place plants in growing tubes and suspend them into water
use pest and disease-free seedlings, and planting material for the establishment of hydroponic crops
maintain a reservoir to hold the nutrient solution and pump it as per the requirement to the tubes of growing plants
automate the nutrient flow system using the cyclic monitoring application, as required
use non-circulating methods for nutrient application, where applicable, such as root dipping technique, floating technique, capillary action technique, etc.
ensure the availability of adequate lighting for the optimum growth of plants in the hydroponic system through the use of a relevant lighting system, such as the solar lighting system

modules.module_title: Maintain the hydroponic system and plants/ crop

pcs.pc_description: check the pipes for any salt deposits and remove it safely to prevent choking and ensure the nutrient solution flows without obstruction through the pipes
check and ensure that the roots of plants get an appropriate quantity of nutrient solution for healthy growth
drain out the rainwater from the site to ensure no waterlogging
clean and monitor the condition of motors controlling water tanks, pumps, and growing trays
use clean water in the hydroponic system and maintain the pH level of the water by using the recommended treatment
clean the floor and maintain it dry in the hydroponic system
detect pests and diseases and take appropriate remedial measures
position the grains appropriately on growing trays to prevent waterlogging in them
soak good quality grains as per the requirement and use an appropriate time- management technique to avoid over-soaking of grains
use mesh filters for regular cleaning
carry out manual or auto-misting of the crop and plants with water to prevent the harmful effects of temperature
use nets for aeration and to prevent birds and animals from preying on the plants/ crop
check the pH using a pH meter regularly and follow the recommended practices to adjust it to the required level in the hydroponic system and nutrient solution, as required
maintain the recommended nutrient solution temperature, and take appropriate measures to control the temperature
use the oxygen meter with mobile application support and alarm to monitor the level of dissolved oxygen in the nutrient solution and follow the recommended practices to maintain or adjust it
maintain the recommended air space between the nutrient solution and the roots of plants
clean the hydroponic system regularly using chlorine or other recommended treatment, and flush the system with clean water before replanting
use auto-cleaning systems for cleaning in large-scale hydroponic systems to save time and achieve better productivity
ensure the required macro and micronutrients are available to plants and crops according to different stages of their growth
maintain hygiene along with the recommended temperature and Relative Humidity (RH) at the site of hydroponic farming by following the recommended practices, such as the use of exhaust fans
carry out artificial pollination using blowers, and use mechanical vibrators to improve air quality within the protected hydroponic system structures
install artificial supporting structures and train tall-growing intermediate crop varieties such as tomatoes and cucumber, and crops bearing heavy produce such as bell pepper, eggplant, etc.
tie strings at the base of each plant with an appropriate material such as polythene
carry out pruning of plants using the appropriate tools and implements, when required
carry out irrigation of plants either manually or using the drip irrigation system, as per the irrigation schedule
determine the amount of fertilisers to be used for fertigation based on the selected crop, its stages of growth, and the type of selected hydroponics technique
select the relevant fertigation technique for use, as appropriate
mix the appropriate fertilisers with the daily water requirement and apply it manually or by using a fertigation system/nutrient tank, according to the selected fertigation technique
maintain the record of irrigation and fertigation of crop

pcs.pc_description: sterilise the relevant equipment and containers using an alcohol-based disinfectant
pour sterile water into the container with the plant parts
shake the container gently after placing a sterile lid to wash the tissue and remove the sterilising solution
place the plant parts using sterilised gloves on a sterile petri dish after removing from the container
cut the plant parts into smaller pieces of the recommended length using a sterilised blade
discard the damaged plant parts safely
place the plant pieces into the culture bottles/ tubes containing culture medium using sterile forceps
place cap on the culture bottles/ tubes tightly
store the culture bottles/ tubes in trays or storage racks safely
maintain the appropriate conditions in the lab such as temperature, humidity and illumination for the multiplication of plant tissues
add cytokinin to the culture medium as per the requirement to regulate the growth of plant shoots
monitor the plant shoots regularly for the correct growth and any contaminations
discard the contaminated plant shoots as per the SOP
transfer the proliferated shoots to fresh culture medium for mass multiplication
place the shoots in another nutrient culture medium specific for root development
add auxins in the recommended quantity to promote root formation
monitor the development of roots
apply the necessary treatment to resolve any issues with root development
maintain the record of observations in the register or the relevant computer system
select a facility with the appropriate temperature and humidity favourable for the plants
remove the plantlets from culture bottles/ tubes after they achieve adequate growth and rooting
wash the plantlets gently to remove any traces of culture media
plant the tissue cultured plants in micro-pots filled with soil/ soilrite/ sand for primary hardening
label the plants with the necessary information
apply water and fertilizers in the recommended quantity as per the schedule
maintain the plants in the facility for the recommended duration before hardening off
place the plants in a greenhouse or shade net facility with controlled micro-climatic conditions such as relative humidity, temperature, light intensity and air circulation
transfer the plants to larger pots for secondary hardening after they develop new leaves and roots
maintain the level of nutrients for the optimum growth of plants
conduct routine checks on the plantlets to ensure their healthy growth and detect presence of any infections
remove the dead and decaying plants
maintain the plants in the environment for the recommended period before transplanting

pcs.pc_description: select a site with ample sunlight, distant from low lying area and suitable environmental conditions for flower crop under protected cultivation
select commercially viable varieties of flowers that can be grown under protected cultivation in the selected site such as rose, gerbera, carnation, anthurium, lilium, orchids, chrysanthemum, etc.
set up structure for protected cultivation based on types of flower crop, conditions to be altered, output volumes, budgets and resources available, etc.
apply measures to test and alter the environmental conditions within the protected cultivation structure based on the requirements of the flower crop
select appropriate soil or soilless medium for the flower crop
prepare the media to have appropriate pH, porosity, moisture retention, salinity, organic content and anchorage as required for the flower crop
decontaminate the media using methods such as chemical drenching/ fumigation, steaming, pasteurization and solarization
ensure flat planting bed for flowers
select planting material like, seeds or saplings, tissue cultured plantlets based on the flower variety and planting medium
apply appropriate propagation method for the flower crop such as shield or T-budding, stenting method, cuttings, micro-propagation
prepare the planting material such as seeds, seedlings or cuttings
plant the planting material maintaining the right spacing to ensure optimum planting density
prepare daily/weekly irrigation and fertigation schedule as per the requirement of the crop
apply appropriate micro-irrigation techniques including use of fertigation equipment, spraying system, exhaust fan and cooling pads as per the stage of growth of the flower crop
ensure good quality of filtered water for flower crop
manage weeds using appropriate method
prepare and apply appropriate dose of manure fertilizer as per crop requirement
apply micro-nutrients by foliar spray
carry out centering (or decentering), to promote the growth of auxiliary buds and lateral branches as per the requirement of the plant using wired nets
trim the growing branches for further lateral branch formation, good spread and budding surface
prune and trim the terminal of the plants as per their cycle
carry out the plant management practices of pinching, disbudding, de-shooting, defoliation, removal of faded flowers and bending of shoots as per plant requirement
identify indicators of disease, infestation, disorder and damage to the flower crop
apply appropriate measures for prevention and treatment of disease, infestation, disorder and damage to the flower crop
select appropriate harvesting practices of loose and cut flower
harvest the flowers as per the market requirement in terms of stage of harvest, stem length, bud size, quality and quantity of produce, type of packaging, etc.
pack the flowers for temporary storage
use weighing machine to accurately weigh the produce
sort and grade the harvested produce based on quality, colour, stem strength and size
process the segregated produce which are not meeting the quality standards
pack, store and transport the marketable produce, ensuring that the produce remains fresh and damage free for a long time
record the details of harvest and post- harvest activities in the desired format
